title: Do Technical Indicators Improve Deep Learning Forecasts? An Empirical Ablation Study Across Asset Classes
content: The effectiveness of conventional technical indicators in deep learning-based financial forecasting remains an open empirical question.  This study presents a large-scale ablation analysis of their contribution to next-day price prediction using recurrent neural networks.  We conduct 500 controlled experiments across 10 assets representing five asset classes: commodities, cryptocurrencies, equities, foreign exchange, and market indices, using daily OHLCV data from 2010 to 2025.  Five feature configurations are evaluated: raw OHLCV inputs and four indicator-augmented variants incorporating momentum, trend, volatility, and all indicators.  Each configuration is assessed using LSTM and GRU architectures across five random seeds.  Results demonstrate that technical indicators generally fail to improve forecasting performance and frequently increase prediction errors.  The raw OHLCV baseline achieves the lowest mean RMSE (\(0.166 \pm 0.148\)) and highest mean directional accuracy (\(55.7\% \pm 5.5\%\)).  The comprehensive indicator configuration increases RMSE by \(34.6\%\) (\(p < 0.001\), Cohen's \(d = -0.29\)), while all four indicator categories exhibit statistically significant performance degradation at \(\alpha = 0.05\).  GRU models achieve higher directional accuracy than LSTM models (\(55.3\%\) versus \(51.0\%\)), although their RMSE difference is not statistically significant (\(p = 0.846\)).  Foreign exchange is the only asset class benefiting from volatility indicators, with a \(4.2\%\) RMSE reduction, whereas cryptocurrencies and commodities exhibit \(83\%\) higher mean prediction error than lower-volatility assets.  These findings suggest that recurrent networks may implicitly learn patterns represented by conventional indicators, rendering explicit indicator features redundant or detrimental.  The results underscore the importance of rigorous baseline comparisons and evidence-driven feature selection in neural network-based financial forecasting.
